questions.question: SDXL won't render a crystal instead of a head from a prompt. How do you want to get the crystal head while keeping the character consistent?

options.label: Inpaint it in SDXL
options.description: Keep your exact hand-drawn pen-flow style: render the figure, mask the head region, and paint a faceted crystal into it (the mask forces what the prompt can't). Preserves the look you locked. Scaling to wild action poses needs auto head-detection per frame — a moderate build. (Recommended — keeps your style)

options.label: Switch to FLUX for this character
options.description: FLUX renders unusual concepts like a crystal head faithfully — but cleaner/more vector (the look you didn't like). We'd push it rougher or post-process toward hand-drawn. Trades your ink texture for concept accuracy.

options.label: Train a crystal-head LoRA
options.description: Make a handful of crystal-head reference frames (via inpaint or FLUX), train a small character model, then it renders the crystal head IN your SDXL hand-drawn style across any pose. Strongest + most reusable — but the most setup (this is Track II).

options.label: Prototype inpaint first
options.description: Before committing, let me inpaint a crystal onto one of the great standing figures we already have (cheap, local, ~3 min) so you can SEE the SDXL-inpaint crystal head in your style and judge it.

# BLUELINE — Full Accounting + Coherence Reset

## Context — why this change

BLUELINE was built the way the palace likes: many threads pulled individually, each a
self-contained proof that ships a capability. That worked — the pipeline is real and mostly
proven — but the *coordination surface* has drifted out of sync with the *work*. Concretely, as
of 2026-07-03 the project is:

- **~26 proof folders** under `Projects/BLUELINE/proofs/` (413 MB in `blender-handdrawn` alone),
- **7 overlapping coordination docs** (`Production Plan`, `Production Pipeline`,
  `Specialists and Seams`, `Render Backend`, `Board Record Schema`, `Deposit Map`, `toolbox`)
  plus a stale `baton` and a `superseded` `Claude Code Job`,
- **~13 pod-orchestrator scripts** scattered across proof folders, several reinventing
  boot/terminate/transport that the hardened `render-backend/runner.py` + `_ops/commons` already solve,
- **3 stranded feature branches** carrying real unmerged threads *(you are reconciling these in
  parallel — this plan assumes they land clean on main: Track VI elemental-motion,
  Line-Art Layer Decomposition + blender-fire, Text Layer / Living Balloon)*.

Nobody entering cold can tell which doc is authoritative, where a capability lives, what's proven
vs retired, or which orchestrator to call. **Goal: one coherent, searchable, manageable set of
tools and processes, reset for the next big lift — with the Motion & Flow subsystem (figures/posing
→ movement → flow field) unified and pushed forward as the centerpiece.**

Decisions locked (2026-07-03): **Medium** depth (reorganize + consolidate, don't extract a new
repo); branches **assumed clean on main**; **Motion & Flow unification first.**

---

## The accounting — where each thread stands, and how they're out of sync

### Proven & merged on main (the solid floor)
| Thread | State | Home |
|---|---|---|
| Clock & sync (Track III) | ✅ SHIPPED, live-validated on *Ascension_v8* (120 BPM → 12 fr/beat) | `proofs/track-III-clock/`, `proofs/animatic/` |
| Rendered-board animatic | ✅ verified live | `proofs/animatic/` |
| M0 previz · M1 comic-register · M2 motion-comic | ✅ verified | `proofs/m0-previz` · `m1-animatic` · `m2-motion-comic` |
| 6-shot noir-tragedy storyboard | ✅ complete | `proofs/new-story/` |
| Conditioning keystone (Blocked, Not Prompted) | ✅ proven | Shop/Blender + `session-1` |
| Figure & pose (Figure Rig Specialist) | ✅ mature — MPFB2/Rigify native rig, **hands shipped**, face next | `Shop/Figure Rig.md`; scripts in `proofs/blender-handdrawn/followups/rig-openpose/` |
| Character-aware flow field | ✅ first proof (2026-07-02) — field bends around a posed figure | `proofs/session-4-figure-flow/` |
| Style lock (`pen-flow`) + style atlas | ✅ locked; 47-frame Phase-2 atlas | `proofs/style-lock/`, `proofs/style-atlas/` |
| Text layer rung 1 (material register) | ✅ proven | `proofs/text-layer/`, `BLUELINE — Text Layer.md` |
| Render backend (Study=SDXL/pod, Piece=FLUX/serverless) | ✅ operational | `BLUELINE — Render Backend.md`, `render-backend/` |
| Toolbox (env pin manifest) | ✅ current (2026-07-02) | `BLUELINE — toolbox.md` |

### Honest negatives (retired — do not reinvest)
- **Render-noise flow-warp (Track V / M3→M3.7):** flow-warped noise **never beats seed-lock** at the
  render, across every regime (single jump 48–483 px and cumulative sequence). The "move the noise
  at the render" sub-claim of *The Flow Field is the Spine* is **retired**; the field survives as the
  **compositional/FX spine**, not a render-noise tool. `proofs/m3-warped-noise/` (5 reports).
- **Character LoRA (Track II):** scored below its text-only baseline (learned a hooded costume, not a
  face). Pipeline sound (DreamBooth control +0.35); style LoRA is the live asset. Identity → InstantID.
- **Crystal-head character:** base SDXL refuses it; deferred to inpaint/FLUX-ref/LoRA.

### Landing from branches (your parallel cleanup → main)
- **Track VI elemental-motion** — smoke/plume Blender sims + optical-flow + velocity-warp + a reusable
  `lib/` (pod/comfy/warp/fields/stylize). **A whole new motion track not in any plan doc.**
- **Line-Art Layer Decomposition** (`Line-Art Layer Decomposition.md` + `proofs/blender-fire/`) —
  convert-first flat-cel → SAM/Depth-Anything/LaMa segment/depth/infill → stylize back. Validated.
- **Text Layer / Living Balloon** — balloon×gen-AI (bubble+word as one gen-AI material), 12-style
  catalog, plus a multi-agent-safe balloon pod orchestrator + canny readiness gate.

### The out-of-sync / racing-ahead findings (what the reset fixes)
1. **The plan docs describe Tracks I–V + stages 0–7, but reality grew past them.** Track VI exists
   off-book; Text Layer and Line-Art Decomposition are whole sub-projects with no place in the
   pipeline map; Figure Rig matured into its own Specialist while Production Plan Track IV still
   calls the Bench nascent; Frame Designer spawned out and partly supersedes `Specialists and Seams`.
2. **The Motion/Flow story is split across 5 non-cross-referencing locations** — session-3 (blind
   field), session-4 (character-aware), M2 (field-in-comic scroll), Track V/M3 (retired render-noise),
   Track VI (elemental sims). `flow-field-spine.md` is the closest hub but predates session-4 **and**
   Track VI. There is no single "here's what's proven / retired / next" for motion.
3. **Tooling fragmentation:** ~13 orchestrators, each with its own boot/terminate; the hard-won
   multi-agent safety (`_ops/runpod/agent_ns.py`, `_ops/commons/` reaper·lease·endpoint) and the
   canonical `render-backend/runner.py` aren't uniformly used. Figure Rig (Shop canon) points its
   scripts *into* a BLUELINE proof folder — a location inversion.
4. **Doc status fields are inconsistent** (`draft`/`adopted`/`proposal`/`active`/`superseded` with no
   rule), and `BLUELINE.md`'s "Where it stands" has become a 15-paragraph de-facto status log that
   nobody can scan.

---

## The reset — recommended approach (Medium)

Four workstreams. **W4 (Motion & Flow) is the priority and can start first**; W1–W3 are the coherence
scaffolding it lands into.

### W1 · One front door: the BLUELINE Atlas
Create **`Projects/BLUELINE/BLUELINE — Atlas.md`** — the single "you are here" status map and search
index. It is the `plan`-type bundle work-state SCHEMA §8 defines but BLUELINE never got. Contents:
- The **8 subsystems** (below), each as a row: one-line charter · state (proven/partial/retired/next)
  · canonical doc · proof folders · orchestrator/scripts.
- A **proof-dir → subsystem** table so every one of the ~26 folders is placed (searchability without
  moving 400 MB).
- A short **"retired, do not reinvest"** list (render-noise warp, character LoRA, crystal-head).

Then **trim `BLUELINE.md`'s "Where it stands"** to a 2–3 sentence status + a link to the Atlas
(git holds the long-form history).

**The 8 subsystems (the searchable taxonomy):**
1. **Clock & Sync** — Track III transport/clip-scan, OSC→WS relay, (bar,beat)→frame determinism, animatic player.
2. **Board Record & Staging** — the contract (`Board Record Schema`), staging-spec, staging-skeleton, Seam A/B.
3. **Figure & Pose** — `Shop/Figure Rig` (MPFB2/Rigify, hands, face-next), pose library + camera-grammar solvers, plate emission, D2 redraw, Freestyle/toon hand-drawn look.
4. **Motion & Flow** ← centerpiece — flow-field spine, character-aware field, field-in-comic, elemental sims; render-noise **retired**.
5. **Render Backend** — Study(SDXL/pod)/Piece(FLUX/serverless), the runner + node-title contract, orchestrators, Commons multi-agent safety, toolbox.
6. **Style & Identity** — `pen-flow` lock, Taste Breeder, style-atlas, Visual Language Console, LoRA Trainer, InstantID face-slot/gaze.
7. **Text & Lettering** — Text Layer, `Shop/Lettering`, balloon catalog, Living Balloon, 2.5D Paper Stack.
8. **Line-Art Decomposition** — convert-first flat-cel → SAM/Depth-Anything/LaMa → stylize back.

### W2 · Reconcile the coordination docs (7 → a clear hierarchy)
- **Keep as canonical:** `Production Pipeline` (the conceptual stage map 0–7 + the two seams),
  `Render Backend`, `Board Record Schema`, `toolbox`. Normalize their `status:` to `active`.
- **Fold into the Atlas, then mark `status: historical`:** `Production Plan` (its Tracks I–V are now
  subsystems) and `Specialists and Seams` (its "how many Specialists" question is answered by the
  live Figure Rig / Lettering / Frame Designer entries). Migrate any still-live content up first.
- **Archive to `Projects/BLUELINE/Archive/`:** `Deposit Map` (proposal, executed) and
  `Claude Code Job` (superseded). Git keeps history.
- **Delete the stale `baton`** (2026-06-23 storyboard→animatic — the animatic shipped) per the Baton
  Ceremony; git is the archive.

### W3 · Consolidate the tooling (one runner, safe by default, findable scripts)
- **Anoint the canonical render/orchestration layer:** `render-backend/runner.py` + `pod_runner.py`
  + `serverless_runner.py`, riding `_ops/runpod/agent_ns.py` (per-agent slug) and `_ops/commons/`
  (`reaper.py` `--self`, `lease.py`, `endpoint.py`). Document this as *the* entry point in the Atlas.
- **Audit the ~13 proof orchestrators** (`pose_pod_orchestrator`, `balloon_pod_orchestrator`,
  `sdxl_/flux_/m3_orchestrator`, `instantid_orchestrator`, `batch_pod`/`batch_hands_pod`/`batch_faces_pod`,
  `m3.6/m3.7_pod_render`): tag each **superseded** (→ point to the canonical runner) or **still-used**
  (→ verify it imports `agent_ns` + reaps its own namespace). Record the verdicts in the Atlas; do not
  mass-delete working proofs.
- **Fix the Figure Rig location inversion:** move (or symlink + note) the rig scripts from
  `proofs/blender-handdrawn/followups/rig-openpose/` into a stable `Shop/Figure Rig/` bundle, and
  update the Specialist's `Tools:` pointer. Keep the toolbox doc as the reproduce-anchor.

### W4 · Unify Motion & Flow, and design the next lift (PRIORITY — start here)
Create **`Projects/BLUELINE/BLUELINE — Motion and Flow.md`** (canonical subsystem doc, type `meta`)
that consolidates the 5 split threads with honest per-thread status, **absorbs/retires the stale
`flow-field-spine.md`** (it predates session-4 and Track VI), and states the unifying design:

> **The flow field is the meeting point of pose, movement, and the song clock.** Today those three
> are separate degrees of freedom; the next lift is to *couple* them through the field.

Three coupling edges, in priority order (each traceable to an existing proof + its named honest limit):
1. **pose → field (nearest, ingredients exist).** Derive the obstacle mask from the *same board-record
   pose* that conditions the render, so obstacle-figure ≡ rendered-figure by construction (session-4
   honest-limit #3). Reuses Figure Rig's depth/openpose plates + `session-4-figure-flow/field.py`.
   Plus the two already-named concrete next steps: **flow-field-biased ink splatter**
   (`blender-handdrawn` Part-4 hook — blobs proven in 3D, bias not yet wired) and **feed the field to
   the render** (session-4 limit #5: the low-denoise img2img fuse into one ink drawing).
2. **field → clock (the big lift).** Make the field a function of the song playhead — a **time-varying
   field that evolves per beat** (flow-field-spine.md's named "next escalation"), so dust actually
   blows through the shot and speed-lines shift on accents. This is the seam that joins Motion & Flow
   to **Clock & Sync (Track III)** and pairs with *Move the Ink, Don't Redraw It*. Fold **Track VI
   elemental-motion**'s `lib/` (fields/warp/optical_flow) in here as the sim substrate.
3. **field → figure motion (a decision, not yet a build).** Interpolate held key-poses along the flow
   direction. **Blocked today by the "staged, not simulated" scope lock** — surface it to Loudon as an
   explicit keep/relax decision rather than silently building it.

Then update the concept entry **`The Flow Field is the Spine`**: record the retired render-noise
sub-claim and the character-aware promotion ("the wind now knows the body is there"), and bump its
stage `sprout → growing`.

---

## Critical files

**Create**
- `Projects/BLUELINE/BLUELINE — Atlas.md` — front-door status map + subsystem/proof index (W1).
- `Projects/BLUELINE/BLUELINE — Motion and Flow.md` — unified motion subsystem + the 3 coupling edges (W4).
- `Projects/BLUELINE/Archive/` — holds retired `Deposit Map` + `Claude Code Job`.

**Edit**
- `Projects/BLUELINE/BLUELINE.md` — trim "Where it stands" to a summary + Atlas link; add subsystem links; fold in Track VI / Line-Art / Text-Layer threads.
- `The Flow Field is the Spine.md` — retired sub-claim + character-aware promotion; stage bump.
- `Projects/BLUELINE/flow-field-spine.md` — mark superseded-by / fold into Motion and Flow.
- `Projects/BLUELINE/BLUELINE — Production Plan.md`, `BLUELINE — Specialists and Seams.md` — `status: historical`, redirect to Atlas.
- `Projects/BLUELINE/BLUELINE — Production Pipeline.md` — add Text Layer, Line-Art Decomposition, Track VI as stages/branches so the map is complete; `status: active`.
- `Shop/Figure Rig.md` — repoint `Tools:` to the relocated stable bundle path.
- Normalize `status:` across the `BLUELINE — *.md` set.

**Reuse (do not rebuild)**
- `render-backend/runner.py`, `pod_runner.py`, `serverless_runner.py` — canonical runner.
- `_ops/runpod/agent_ns.py`, `_ops/commons/{reaper,lease,endpoint,provider}.py` — multi-agent safety.
- `proofs/session-4-figure-flow/field.py`, `proofs/track-VI-elemental-motion/lib/` — the motion substrate.
- `BLUELINE — toolbox.md`, `BLUELINE — Board Record Schema.md` — the reproduce + contract anchors.

**Optional physical grouping (medium, low-risk):** cluster the Motion & Flow proofs under
`proofs/motion-flow/` (session-3, session-4, track-V, track-VI) since that's the priority subsystem;
leave everything else index-only to avoid 400 MB of git churn.

---

## Verification
1. **Coverage check:** a scan confirms every folder in `proofs/` and every `render-backend/` + orchestrator script appears exactly once in the Atlas's proof→subsystem table (no orphans).
2. **Link integrity:** all new/edited `[[wikilinks]]` resolve; run `_ops/swarm/lint-doc-drift.py` and the entry-naming lint clean.
3. **Doc hierarchy:** exactly the four canonical coordination docs remain `status: active`; `Production Plan` + `Specialists and Seams` read `historical` and link to the Atlas; `Deposit Map`/`Claude Code Job` are in `Archive/`; the stale `baton` is gone.
4. **Tooling:** the Atlas names one canonical runner; every orchestrator is tagged superseded-or-still-used; any still-used one is confirmed to import `agent_ns` and reap its own namespace (`python3 _ops/runpod/test_multi_agent.py` still passes).
5. **Motion & Flow doc:** every status claim traces to a real proof file; the 3 coupling edges each cite their source proof + honest limit; `The Flow Field is the Spine` reflects the retired render-noise result.
6. **(Gated, costs GPU) end-to-end smoke:** drive one board record through the canonical runner to confirm the consolidation didn't break the render path — run only on your go, since it spends RunPod credit.

fresh cold-entrant test confirmed: "where it stands" is clear (~15 min), but "what's next" took 45+

marked `historical`, and `BLUELINE.md` still opens with a stale 2026-06-24 banner.

**"production plan"** knows exactly what they'll get. So the right move is not a new-named doc — it's

current front door**, `status: active`. It answers, in this order, exactly what you named:

   surreal-mathematical music-video action; storyboard → animatic → render, every frame pinned to a
   fixed-tempo song; the bias is the product. (from the entry + Deposit Map thesis.)

   humanoid-only; each milestone ships; the end state = a full song, end to end, as an instrument).

   Track I–VI lineage where it maps:
   Clock & Sync · Board Record & Staging · Figure & Pose · **Motion & Flow** · Render Backend ·
   Style & Identity · Text & Lettering · Line-Art Decomposition.
5. **Next steps / the horizon** — one prioritized cross-thread stack (the piece that was missing),
   in three buckets + a gate:
   - *Ready now:* Motion&Flow Edge 1 (pose→field: ink-splatter + field-to-render); Figure&Pose face

   - *Gate:* full-song production volume once a board pair survives motion + boards leveled + a muxed cut.

   substrate-first framing from the old plan (so the reasoning isn't lost).

## Retire "Atlas" (fold it in, remove the confusing name)
- Move the Atlas's content into the revised Production Plan (threads table, proof→thread map, retired list).
- **Delete `BLUELINE — Atlas.md`** and repoint its inbound `[[BLUELINE — Atlas]]` links →
  `[[BLUELINE — Production Plan]]` in: `BLUELINE.md`, `BLUELINE — Motion and Flow.md`,
  `The Flow Field is the Spine.md`, `BLUELINE — Render Backend.md`, `BLUELINE — Production Pipeline.md`.

## Also
- **`BLUELINE.md`** — replace the stale 2026-06-24 STATUS banner with a current one-liner pointing at
  the Production Plan as the front door; fix the Bundle list (Production Plan = read-first; drop the
  Atlas row; add "new here? skip the historical/archived docs"). Repoint the frontmatter link.
- **`BLUELINE — Motion and Flow.md`** — Edge 3 clarity ("a one-line scope call, not a research
  blocker; ready to build if relaxed").
- **`BLUELINE — toolbox.md`** — clarify "Serverless (future)" is the planned Piece-tier path, not a
  current blocker.

## Files
- Rewrite `Projects/BLUELINE/BLUELINE — Production Plan.md` (historical → active front door).
- Delete `Projects/BLUELINE/BLUELINE — Atlas.md`; repoint the 5 inbound links above.
- Edit `Projects/BLUELINE/BLUELINE.md`, `BLUELINE — Motion and Flow.md`, `BLUELINE — toolbox.md`.

## Execution + verification
- Work in the `feature/blueline-horizon` worktree (already created), commit with explicit pathspecs,
  merge `--no-ff` to main, tear down.
- Verify: `_ops/swarm/lint-doc-drift.py` clean; **no `[[BLUELINE — Atlas]]` link remains**; the stale
  2026-06-24 banner is gone; every next-steps item links its owning thread doc; a quick re-read
  confirms the Production Plan alone answers what/where/goals/threads/next.

## Context — the re-assessment, and the correction

You asked whether a newcomer would know **where BLUELINE stands** and **where the horizon is**. A
fresh cold-entrant test confirmed: "where it stands" is clear (~15 min), but "what's next" took 45+
min of spelunking with no unified roadmap — the forward-plan got orphaned when the Production Plan was
marked `historical`, and `BLUELINE.md` still opens with a stale 2026-06-24 banner.

**Your correction (the important one):** the fix I proposed put the status/horizon in a doc named
**"Atlas"** — but that's a coinage a newcomer wouldn't think to search for. Someone searching
**"production plan"** knows exactly what they'll get. So the right move is not a new-named doc — it's
to **revive and rewrite `BLUELINE — Production Plan.md`** as the single, clear, current front-door
document, and fold the Atlas into it.

## The deliverable — one rewritten `BLUELINE — Production Plan.md`

Rewrite the doc in place (currently `status: historical`, track-based, stale) into the **canonical
current front door**, `status: active`. It answers, in this order, exactly what you named:

   surreal-mathematical music-video action; storyboard → animatic → render, every frame pinned to a
   fixed-tempo song; the bias is the product. (from the entry + Deposit Map thesis.)
2. **Goals** — the destination and the locked scope decisions (fixed tempo; staged-not-simulated;
   humanoid-only; each milestone ships; the end state = a full song, end to end, as an instrument).
3. **Where it stands** — the status: the **threads** (below) with each marked proven / partial /
   retired, plus the retired-do-not-reinvest list. (folds in the Atlas's subsystem table + proof map.)
4. **The threads** — the 8 working threads (what each is · state · canonical doc · proof folders).
   These are the current parts of the project; I'll use your word **"threads,"** noting the historical
   Track I–VI lineage where it maps:
   Clock & Sync · Board Record & Staging · Figure & Pose · **Motion & Flow** · Render Backend ·
   Style & Identity · Text & Lettering · Line-Art Decomposition.
